name: 21193-sharegpt-qwen3moe30b-2gpu
hardware: 2x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 of ONE a3 node (--gres=gpu:2), sm90, NVLink between the two cards. Driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: DP=2, TP=1, PP=1 with expert parallelism ON: two engine ranks, one per GPU, so the 128 routed experts of each layer land 64 per rank and no expert is split. Not substitutable -- the same two cards at `-tp 2` with DP=1 take an entirely different expert implementation.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), 1000 streams, bounded at 2000 requests with a 900 s safety cap, warmup the first 25% and cooldown the last 10%. Warmup is a percent of the request bound while cooldown is a percent of the duration budget, so 1500 requests are measured and the cooldown discards nothing at this cap. The stream count is a seed, but the whole population in flight is the operating point this item is defined at: a run far below it is a different regime and should be recorded as one.
workload: guidellm `json_file` over `configs/data/sharegpt-1000-qwen3moe30b.jsonl`: 1000 ShareGPT conversations, 217393 prompt tokens and 201847 output tokens in total. Requests are very uneven -- prompt tokens mean 217.4, p50 85, max 1007; output tokens mean 201.8, p50 148, max 872. Per-row `output_tokens_count` is enforced and sampling is temperature 0.0, so every run generates the identical 201847 tokens; `request_format: plain` applies no chat template; prefix caching is off and the conversations are independent first turns. `configs/data/make-dataset.py` regenerates the file from the local ShareGPT JSON and asserts both totals.
purpose: A mixture-of-experts chat assistant on two GPUs, serving a thousand concurrent open-ended conversations of a few hundred tokens each.
launch:
# The engine's command line, for the commit named by configs/setupcard.md.
#
# CAUTION, flat reader: this file is read line by line, indented lines are skipped and a value is
# truncated at the first `#`, so every key must be top-level and every value must fit on one line.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8
trust-remote-code: true

# The topology the item is defined at, and it may not be recast: the MoE all-to-all path is gated
# on data parallelism plus expert parallelism, so `-tp 2` with DP=1 takes a different expert path.
# `FusedMoEParallelConfig.use_all2all_kernels` is literally `dp_size > 1 and use_ep`, so DP=2 is
# the mechanism, not a packaging choice.
#
# THE VALUE BELOW IS A GPU-COUNT DECLARATION, NOT THE TOPOLOGY THAT RUNS. Under a harness that
# sizes the GPU allocation from this one key alone, with no notion of data parallelism, declaring
# the truthful `1` here hands a DP=2 engine a single GPU, and DP rank 1 dies in
# `_init_data_parallel` with `IndexError: list index out of range` before serving one request.
# So this key carries the number of GPUs the item needs (2), and the harness puts the engine back
# to the real `tensor-parallel-size: 1` after the allocation is chosen. The engine therefore runs
# DP=2 x TP=1 x EP=2 on two cards, exactly as the source did. To start it by hand from this file,
# pass `--tensor-parallel-size 1` in place of this value.
tensor-parallel-size: 2
data-parallel-size: 2
enable-expert-parallel: true

enable-prefix-caching: false

# Pinned per rank, not redundant: an engine constructed in-process falls through to SchedulerConfig's
# own much smaller values, which changes the batch shape the item is measured at.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

max-model-len: 4096
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
